The '''2020–21 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Michigan]] during the [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]].  This season marked the program's 105th season and its 104th consecutive year as a member of the [[Big Ten Conference]]. The Wolverines, led by second-year head coach [[Juwan Howard]], played their home games for the 54th consecutive year at the [[Crisler Center]] in [[Ann Arbor, Michigan]].

The Wolverines finished the season with a 23–5 record, including a 14–3 conference record, to win its first Big Ten championship since [[2013–14 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2014]]. The team earned a one seed in the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]], where they reached the Elite Eight before losing to [[2020–21 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|UCLA]].

==Previous season==
The [[2019–20 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Wolverines]] finished the [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2019–20 season]] 19–12, including 10–10 in [[2019–20 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten play]]. Michigan was scheduled to face [[2019–20 Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball team|Rutgers]] in the second round of the [[2020 Big Ten men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]]; however, on March 12, 2020, the Big Ten canceled the tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2020/3/12/mens-basketball-big-ten-cancels-remainder-of-big-ten-tournament.aspx |title=Big Ten Cancels Remainder of Conference men's basketball tournament |access-date=March 19, 2020 |date=March 12, 2020 |website=MGoBlue.com |publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]}}</ref> Also on March 12, the NCAA announced the cancellation of the [[2020 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], along with all remaining winter and spring championships, due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.ncaa.org/about/resources/media-center/news/ncaa-cancels-remaining-winter-and-spring-championships |title=NCAA cancels remaining winter and spring championships |publisher=NCAA |date=March 12, 2020 |access-date=March 19, 2020}}</ref>

===Recruiting classes===

====2020 recruiting class====
On October 23, 2018, Michigan received its first class of 2020 commitment from four-star guard Zeb Jackson of [[Montverde Academy]] in suburban [[Orlando, Florida]]. Jackson had met assistant coach [[DeAndre Haynes]] when he was on the [[Toledo Rockets men's basketball|Toledo]] staff.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/index.ssf/2018/10/four-star_guard_zeb_jackson_co.html|title=Four-star guard Zeb Jackson commits to Michigan basketball|access-date=March 19, 2020|date=October 23, 2018|website=[[MLive.com]]|author=Kahn, Andrew}}</ref> On October 17, 2019, Michigan received its second commitment of the 2020 class and the first commitment of the [[Juwan Howard]] era, five-star [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] [[Isaiah Todd]] of [[Word of God Christian Academy]] in [[Raleigh, North Carolina]]. Todd was the highest-rated recruit to commit to Michigan since 2000 but Todd ended up decommitting from Michigan on April 14, 2020 to instead play in the [[NBA G League]]. Howard then picked up his third commitment of the 2020 class in [[Hunter Dickinson]] a four-star [[Center (basketball)|Center]] out of [[Hyattsville, Maryland]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/2019/10/17/five-star-forward-isaiah-todd-commits-michigan/4008770002/|title='Me and Coach Juwan just click': Five-star forward Isaiah Todd commits to Michigan|last=Hawkins|first=James|website=Detroit News|access-date=March 19, 2020}}</ref> On January 1, 2020, Terrance Williams II, a four-star Forward out of Washington D.C. who de-committed from Georgetown in December 2019, became the fourth commit of the 2020 class.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2020/01/01/michigan-basketball-terrance-williams-commit/2763562001/|title=Michigan basketball lands four-star forward Terrance Williams in 2020 class|last=Sang|first=Orion|website=Detroit Free Press|access-date=March 19, 2020}}</ref> On January 20, Howard picked up his fifth commitment of the 2020 class, his son Jace Howard, a three-star [[small forward]] from [[Miami]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2020/01/20/michigan-basketball-recruiting-jace-howard-commitment/4526803002/|title=Jace Howard, son of Juwan, commits to Michigan basketball|last=Sang|first=Orion|website=Detroit Free Press|date=January 20, 2020|access-date=March 19, 2020}}</ref>

==Regular season==

===November===
Michigan began the season with a 96–82 victory over [[Bowling Green Falcons men's basketball|Bowling Green]]. Michigan was led by Chaundee Brown with 19 points, while [[Isaiah Livers]] added 17 points and nine rebounds, one rebound shy of a [[Double-double (basketball)|double-double]], and [[Mike Smith (basketball, born 1997)|Mike Smith]] added 16 points and eight assists in his Michigan debut.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401262142|title=Newcomers lead No. 25 Michigan to win over Bowling Green|access-date=November 25, 2020|date=November 25, 2020|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2020/11/25/mens-basketball-brown-livers-lead-way-as-u-m-rolls-to-season-opening-win-over-bowling-green.aspx|title=Brown, Livers Lead Way as U-M Rolls to Season-Opening Win over Bowling Green|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|access-date=November 25, 2020|date=November 25, 2020|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref> On November 29, Michigan defeated [[Oakland Golden Grizzlies men's basketball|Oakland]] 81–71 in overtime. Michigan was led by Livers with 22 points, while [[Hunter Dickinson]] scored a career-high 19-points.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401262491|title=No. 25 Michigan outlasts Oakland 81-71 in overtime|access-date=November 29, 2020|date=November 29, 2020|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2020/11/29/mens-basketball-dickinson-livers-lead-michigan-to-overtime-win-against-oakland.aspx|title=Dickinson, Livers Lead Michigan to Overtime Win Against Oakland|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|access-date=November 29, 2020|date=November 29, 2020|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref>

===December===
On December 2, Michigan defeated [[Ball State Cardinals men's basketball|Ball State]] 84–56. Michigan was led by Livers with a game-high 21 points, his second consecutive 20-plus point game, while Dickinson added 12 points and a season-high 11 rebounds for his first career double-double.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401263444|title=Livers scores 21, Michigan beat Ball State 84-65|access-date=December 2, 2020|date=December 2, 2020|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2020/12/2/mens-basketball-livers-dickinson-lead-way-as-michigan-cruises-to-win-over-ball-state.aspx|title=Livers, Dickinson Lead Way as Michigan Cruises to Win over Ball State|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|access-date=December 2, 2020|date=December 2, 2020|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref> On December 6, Michigan defeated [[2020–21 UCF Knights men's basketball team|UCF]] 80–58. Michigan was led by Brown with 18 points, while Dickinson added 14 points and seven rebounds, Eli Brooks added 10 points, and Terrance Williams II added a career-high 10 points and six rebounds. Michigan went on a 22–4 run to end the first half to take their first lead of the game, before closing out the game on a 29–5 run in the second half.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401261568|title=Brown scores 18, Michigan uses big 2nd-half run to beat UCF|access-date=December 6, 2020|date=December 6, 2020|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2020/12/6/mens-basketball-second-half-dominance-leads-michigan-to-victory-over-central-florida.aspx|title=Second-Half Dominance Leads Michigan to Victory Over Central Florida|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|access-date=December 6, 2020|date=December 6, 2020|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref> Michigan was scheduled to face [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|NC State]] in the [[ACC–Big Ten Challenge]] on December 9, however, the game was postponed due to [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19]] concerns within the Wolfpack program.<ref name="ACC-Big Ten Challenge">{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2020/12/7/mens-basketball-michigans-acc-b1g-challenge-matchup-with-north-carolina-state-postponed.aspx |title=Michigan's ACC/B1G Challenge Matchup with North Carolina State Postponed |first=Tom |last=Wywrot |access-date=December 7, 2020 |date=December 7, 2020 |publisher=[[CBS Interactive]] |website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref> It was announced Michigan would then host [[2020–21 Toledo Rockets men's basketball team|Toledo]] for the first time since [[1983–84 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|1983]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2020/12/8/mens-basketball-u-m-to-host-toledo-for-first-time-in-37-years.aspx |title=U-M to Host Toledo for First Time in 37 Years |first=Tom |last=Wywrot |access-date=December 8, 2020 |date=December 8, 2020 |publisher=[[CBS Interactive]] |website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref> Michigan defeated Toledo 91–71. Michigan was led by Dickinson with a game-high 18 points and seven rebounds, while Livers added 16 points, [[Franz Wagner]] added 14 points, and Austin Davis and Brooks added 12 points each.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401268513|title=Dickinson's 18 leads Michigan past Toledo 91-71|access-date=December 9, 2020|date=December 9, 2020|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2020/12/9/mens-basketball-michigan-runs-past-toledo-behind-dickinson-livers.aspx|title=Michigan Runs Past Toledo Behind Dickinson, Livers|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|access-date=December 9, 2020|date=December 9, 2020|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref> On December 13, Michigan defeated [[2020–21 Penn State Nittany Lions basketball team|Penn State]] 62–58 in its [[2020–21 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten Conference season]] opener. ==Postseason==
===Big Ten tournament===
On March 12, Michigan opened its [[2021 Big Ten men's basketball tournament]] play with a 79–66 victory over Maryland in the quarterfinals. Michigan was led by Smith with 18 points and set a Big Ten tournament record with 15 assists, while Wagner and Brooks had 16 points and four rebounds each, and Brown had 10 points. Michigan rallied from a 12-point deficit in the first half, including a 16–2 run to close out the final four minutes of the half, to re-gain the lead they never relinquished. Michigan has won 14 straight tournament openers, the most of any major conference team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2021/3/12/mens-basketball-recap-vs-maryland.aspx|title=Smith, Bench Help Michigan Overcome Slow Start Against Maryland|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|access-date=March 12, 2021|date=March 12, 2021|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref>

The next day Michigan lost to (#9/#10) Ohio State 68–67 in the semifinals of the Big Ten tournament. Michigan was led by Dickinson with 21 points, nine of which came in the final four minutes of the game, while Brooks added 12 points, Smith added 10 points and Wagner added eight points, six rebounds, four assists and two blocks before fouling out late in the second half. Michigan rallied from a 13-point deficit in the second half, including a 11–0 run in the final four minutes of the game, however, their comeback attempt came up short. The Wolverines made a season-best 21 free throws on 23 attempts.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401296333|title=No. 9 Buckeyes edge No. 4 Michigan, make Big Ten title game|access-date=March 13, 2021|date=March 13, 2021|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2021/3/13/mens-basketball-recap-vs-ohio-state.aspx|title=Michigan Comeback Falls Short in Semifinal Against Ohio State|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|access-date=March 13, 2021|date=March 13, 2021|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref>

===NCAA tournament===
On March 20, Michigan began their participation in the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2021 NCAA tournament]] with an 82–66 victory over [[2020–21 Texas Southern Tigers basketball team|Texas Southern]] in the first round. Michigan was led by Smith with 18 points, five assists, four rebounds and one steal, while Dickinson added 16 points and three blocks before fouling out, Brooks and Johns Jr. added 11 points each, and Wagner added nine points, nine rebounds, and a career-high six assists.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2021/3/20/mens-basketball-recap-vs-texas-southern.aspx|title=Smith Leads Balanced U-M Attack in First-Round Win Over Texas Southern|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|access-date=March 20, 2021|date=March 20, 2021|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref>

On March 22, Michigan defeated [[2020–21 LSU Tigers basketball team|LSU]] 86–78 in the second round. Michigan was led by Brown Jr. and Brooks with 21 points each, while Wagner added 15 points and Dickinson added 12 points and 11 rebounds for his sixth career double-double. LSU began the second half with a 9–2 run and regained a six-point lead, 51–45, four minutes into the second period. Michigan then went on a 10–0 run, and regained the lead 55–51. The Tigers responded with a 10–3 run, before the Wolverines used a 14–1 to regain the lead they never relinquished. With the win, the Wolverines advanced to the Sweet Sixteen for the fourth consecutive year, the second-longest active streak, behind [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]] with six.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401310894|title=Big Ten comeback: Michigan topples LSU 86-78|access-date=March 22, 2021|date=March 22, 2021|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2021/3/22/mens-basketball-brooks-brown-provide-scoring-boosts-to-lift-michigan-back-into-sweet-16.aspx|title=Brooks, Brown Provide Scoring Boosts to Lift Michigan Back into Sweet 16|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|access-date=March 22, 2021|date=March 22, 2021|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref>

On March 28, Michigan defeated (#14/#14) [[2020–21 Florida State Seminoles men's basketball team|Florida State]] 76–58 in the Sweet Sixteen. Michigan was led by Johns Jr. with 14 points, six rebounds, two steals and two assists, while Dickinson added 14 points, eight rebounds, two blocks and two assists, Wagner added 13 points and 10 rebounds, for his third double-double of the season, and Brown Jr. added 12 points. Michigan scored 50 percent of its points in the paint and 24 points off turnovers. Michigan's defense held the Seminoles to under 60 points for the first time this season, and forced 14 turnovers. With the win, the Wolverines advanced to the Elite Eight for the fifteenth time in program history and first time since [[2017–18 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2018]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401310874|title=Inside job: Michigan goes to the paint to top FSU 76-58|access-date=March 28, 2021|date=March 28, 2021|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2021/3/28/mens-basketball-quartet-of-double-figure-scorers-stingy-defense-usher-michigan-into-elite-eight.aspx|title=Quartet of Double-Figure Scorers, Stingy Defense Usher Michigan into Elite Eight|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|access-date=March 28, 2021|date=March 28, 2021|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref> The Wolverines would then lose to #11 seed UCLA 51–49, ending their season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2021/3/30/mens-basketball-recap-vs-ucla|title=Michigan Eliminated from NCAA Tournament as Comeback vs. UCLA Falls Short|accessdate=January 11, 2025|date=March 30, 2021|author=Wyrot, Tom|publisher=Board of Regents of the University of Michigan}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2021/03/31/michigan-basketball-ucla-elite-eight/4815071001/|title=Michigan basketball freezes down the stretch in Elite Eight loss to UCLA, 51-49|accessdate=January 11, 2025|date=March 31, 2021|author=Sang, Orion|work=[[Detroit Free Press]]}}</ref>

==Honors==
Following the season [[Juwan Howard]] was named [[Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Coach of the Year|Big Ten Conference Coach of the Year]] while [[Hunter Dickinson]] was named Big Ten Conference Freshman of the Year. Dickinson was also named a first team All-Big Ten selection by the media and a Big Ten All-Freshman honoree, [[Isaiah Livers]] was named a second team All-Big Ten selection by both the coaches and media, and [[Franz Wagner]] was named a second team All-Big Ten selection by the coaches.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://bigten.org/news/2021/3/9/general-2020-21-big-ten-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-announced.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210309180252/https://bigten.org/news/2021/3/9/general-2020-21-big-ten-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-announced.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 9, 2021 |title=2020-21 Big Ten Men’s Basketball Postseason Honors Announced |website=BigTen.org |date=March 9, 2021 |access-date=March 9, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2021/3/9/mens-basketball-dickinson-howard-headline-big-ten-awards-as-top-freshman-coach.aspx |title=Dickinson, Howard Headline Big Ten Awards as Top Freshman, Coach |first=Tom |last=Wywrot |accessdate=March 9, 2021 |date=March 9, 2021 |publisher=[[CBS Interactive]] |website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref>

Multiple Wolverines also earned national honors as well. [[Juwan Howard]] was named the National Coach of the Year by [[Sporting News]] and awarded the [[Henry Iba Award]] by the [[United States Basketball Writers Association|USBWA]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/ncaa-basketball/news/juwan-howard-michigan-coach-of-the-year/1tb73ththc6h41piqjya53s4y5 |title=Michigan's Juwan Howard is Sporting News' 2020-21 Coach of the Year |first=Mike |last=DeCourcy |accessdate=March 9, 2021 |date=March 9, 2021 |publisher=The Sporting News |website=sportingnews.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2021/3/19/mens-basketball-howard-tabbed-as-henry-iba-national-coach-of-the-year-by-usbwa.aspx |title=Howard Tabbed as Henry Iba National Coach of the Year by USBWA |first=Tom |last=Wywrot |accessdate=March 19, 2021 |date=March 19, 2021 |publisher=[[CBS Interactive]] |website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref> [[Hunter Dickinson]] garnered consensus second team [[2021 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] honors, being chosen on the second team by each of the four major selectors. He became Michigan's first consensus All-American since [[Nik Stauskas]] in [[2013–14 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2014]] and 13th all time.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2021/3/16/michigan-mens-basketball-national-honors-2020-21.aspx |title=Dickinson Named to Fourth All-America Second Team List |accessdate=March 16, 2021 |date=March 16, 2021 |publisher=[[CBS Interactive]] |website=MGoBlue.com }}{{Dead link|date=February 2022 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/michigan/Article/Hunter-Dickinson-becomes-Michigan-basketballs-13th-consensus-All-American-just-second-since-1994-162610446/ |title=Hunter Dickinson becomes Michigan's 13th consensus All-American; just second since 1994 |first=Zach |last=Shaw |accessdate=March 18, 2021 |date=March 18, 2021 |website=247sports.com}}</ref>
